regime: Risk-Off Break (Equities Below Falling Stops, Crude Leads)
summary: Risk off day and a clean trend, the mirror image of Monday's coil. Equities sold from the open. NQ closed 29,139, down 1.30 percent and right on the 29,000 psych. MES closed 7,647, down 0.70 percent, losing the 7,700 psych line it sat on Monday. Gold broke hard, down 2.70 percent to 4,342 as the 10 year yield firmed. Crude went the other way and led the board, ripping 5.09 percent to 90.70 and stretching its lead as the only market above a rising stop. Volatility expanded, VIX jumped to 16.34, and jobs week is live with JOLTS mid week and the August payrolls report Friday.
psychology: Trend days are the flip side of chop days. Monday punished anyone who forced trades in a coil. Today punished anyone who tried to fade a one way move. NQ poked above the opening range early, failed, and trended down the rest of the session into the close. When price is below a falling stop and printing lower highs, the higher odds trade is with the trend, not against it. Stop trying to call the bottom on a day like this. Let the tape show you the direction and trade in line with it, or stand aside. The hardest part is doing less when the move looks obvious in hindsight.

event.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August)
event.consensus: Traders came in watching whether the August ISM Manufacturing read would point to cooling growth or add to rate pressure after recent firm data.
event.actual: The ISM Manufacturing print was the scheduled event and the tape sold risk through the session. NQ fell 1.30 percent and MES 0.70 percent, both closing near the session lows. The 10 year yield firmed to about 4.793 from 4.724 and VIX jumped to 16.34 from 14.92, a clear step up in volatility. The exact ISM figure was not captured this run, so the read here is the price reaction, not the release value.
event.surprise: Not captured this run. The pattern lined up with a higher rates read: yields firmed while equities and gold fell together, which is the correlation you see on a rates move rather than a pure growth scare.
event.nqReaction: NQ opened, poked just above the opening range, then trended down the rest of the session to a 29,001 low before a small bounce to close 29,139. A one way trend down day.
event.crossAsset: Crude was the outlier, ripping 5.09 percent to 90.70 and leading the board. Gold fell 2.70 percent to 4,342, unusual on a risk off day and consistent with the firmer yields. The 10 year rose to 4.793 and VIX climbed to 16.34.

risk.sizing: Keep size reduced. Volatility expanded today and stayed elevated into a jobs week, so daily ranges are wider and stops need more room. Equities are trending down below falling stops, that is a with trend short environment, not a place to pick a bottom. Crude is the one clean long, above a rising stop, and can be sized normally with a stop under 88.96.
risk.openRisk: MNQ back above the 29,307 stop or MES above 7,675 on two hourly closes is the first sign the selling is pausing. Below that, the 29,000 psych on NQ and the 7,600 psych on MES are the next downside references. Gold stays weak below 4,391; a reclaim there is the first bounce signal. Crude stays long above 88.96.
risk.note: Jobs week is the driver. JOLTS job openings land mid week and the August payrolls report is Friday Sep 4, with Labor Day the following Monday. Expect wider ranges and headline risk around those prints. Carry reduced size and let the data set the tone. Not financial advice.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN
fullReport.html: HTA OPEN (NY opening range, 13:30 to 13:45 UTC window): OR high 29,140.5, OR low 29,040, width 100.5 points (0.35 percent). Price poked above the OR high right after the open, tagging 29,147 at 13:45 UTC, and pushed to a 29,317 morning high. Then it rolled over and trended down the rest of the session, losing the OR low late at 18:40 UTC (29,014) and printing a 29,001 low before a small bounce to close 29,139, just back inside the range. NYVWAP sat at 29,155 and price closed just under it, so sellers had the day. Signals: an upside fakeout that reversed into a trend down day. HOF (short only) got its direction right on the reversal, but the clean OR low break came late. MID saw a first hour push up then an all session fade. For Wednesday, BIR and BNC are eligible, but HOF and MID are both skipped on Wednesdays under the session rules, so keep any opening range read to the eligible plays.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout
fullReport.html: E3v2 Momentum Long keeps its filter off for the equity index. NQ is below its 29,307 ATR stop and trending down, so a fresh long here fights the tape. The one place momentum is working is crude: MCL broke through 90 on strong follow through and holds above a rising stop, exactly the profile a momentum long looks for. The filter is doing its job on the indices, keeping you out of a long while price is falling, and pointing at the market that is actually trending.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band
fullReport.html: AVWAP deviation band (MNQ): AVWAP center 29,162, close 29,139 is about minus 0.4 sigma, essentially at the mean. Bands: plus 2 sigma 29,289, plus 1 sigma 29,226, minus 1 sigma 29,099, minus 2 sigma 29,035. Sigma widened to 63.5 today from Monday's 43.8 as the range expanded. The reversion read is muted here: on a strong trend day price rode the lower half of the band and the close came back toward the mean rather than tagging an extreme. Volume is unavailable on the continuous contract, so this is price only. The lesson: deviation band fades work best in balance, and today was a trend, so the band was a map of the down move rather than a fade signal.
